debauchery noun

illicit sex, as a disgrace

also illicit sex, fornication, defilement, unchastity, lewdness, seduction, sexual disgrace

classical

Plaut. Amph. 883: stuprī, dēdecoris ā virō argūtam meō
Cic. Tusc. 4.75: stupra et corruptēlae et adulteria, incesta dēnique (Lewis & Short)

stuprum, stuprī n.

noun, second declension

the dishonour of illicit sex: seduction, fornication, rape, as a disgrace to the one dishonoured

In the oldest Latin simply disgrace. Lewis & Short: it always implies dishonour done to the person, man or woman, and is not used of dealings with prostitutes; its opposite is pudīcitia. With force it is rape: stuprum per vim.

Other words

  • impudīcitia, impudīcitiae f. — unchastity, lewdness

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Plaut. Am. 2.2.189 (Lewis & Short); Tac. A. 5.3 (Lewis & Short)

Examples

  • ita mē probrī, stuprī, dēdecoris ā virō argūtam meō!

    to think that my own husband should accuse me so of shame, of unchastity, of disgrace!Plaut. Amph. 882–883

  • hinc pudīcitia, illinc stuprum

    on this side chastity, on that debaucheryCic. Cat. 2.25 (Lewis & Short)

See also rape, violate, adultery, chastity, disgrace, sex.

SourcesLewis & Short: stuprum · Lewis & Short: impudicitia

Plautus, Amphitruo 882–883.
